subject: standard-mathematics
title: Standard Mathematics MYP 5 eAssessment-style Practice Paper 2

questions.content:
An online shop is selling a phone in a sale, and a shop in Paris sells the same phone.

(a) The sale price of the phone is £240, after a reduction of 20%. Calculate the original price. (2 marks)
(b) In Paris the same phone costs €310. The exchange rate is £1 = €1.15. Calculate the price in pounds, correct to the nearest penny. (2 marks)
(c) A transistor in the phone's chip has a width of 0.000 000 007 m. Write this number in standard form. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Method: £240 is 80% (or 0.8) of the original price, so original = 240 ÷ 0.8
[1] £300
Common error: finding 20% of 240 and adding it on, giving £288.
(b)
[1] Method: 310 ÷ 1.15
[1] £269.57 (269.565... before rounding)
Common error: multiplying 310 by 1.15.
(c)
[1] 7 × 10⁻⁹ (accept 7.0 × 10⁻⁹ m)

questions.content:
A designer is making a rectangular poster. The width of the poster is (x + 3) cm and the height is (x + 8) cm.

(a) Expand and simplify (x + 3)(x + 8) to write an expression for the area of the poster. (2 marks)
(b) Factorise fully 4x² + 10x. (2 marks)
(c) Factorise x² − 36. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Method: x² + 8x + 3x + 24 (all four terms correct)
[1] x² + 11x + 24
Common error: x² + 24 (missing the middle terms).
(b)
[1] A common factor of 2x (or 2 or x) is taken out
[1] 2x(2x + 5). Award 1 mark only for a partly factorised answer such as 2(2x² + 5x).
(c)
[1] (x − 6)(x + 6) (accept in either order)

questions.content:
Two gyms offer different plans. Gym A charges a joining fee of £20 plus £15 per month. Gym B has no joining fee but charges £25 per month.

(a) Write a formula for the total cost, C pounds, after m months for each gym. (2 marks)
(b) Solve the two equations simultaneously to find the number of months when the total costs are equal, and state that cost. (2 marks)
(c) Anita plans to join for a full year (12 months). Decide which gym is cheaper and calculate how much she saves. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Gym A: C = 20 + 15m (accept C = 15m + 20)
[1] Gym B: C = 25m
(b)
[1] Method: 20 + 15m = 25m → 20 = 10m → m = 2 months. ECF from (a).
[1] Cost = 25 × 2 = £50 (check: 20 + 15 × 2 = 50). ECF from (a).
(c)
[1] Gym A: 20 + 15 × 12 = £200 and Gym B: 25 × 12 = £300. ECF from (a).
[1] Gym A is cheaper and she saves £100. ECF from (a).
Common error: forgetting the joining fee for Gym A.

questions.content:
A ladder of length 5.5 m leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is on level ground 1.5 m from the base of the wall.

(a) Calculate how high up the wall the ladder reaches. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places. (2 marks)
(b) Calculate the angle between the ladder and the ground. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place. (2 marks)
(c) A safety guide says the angle should be between 70° and 80°. Does the ladder meet this guide? Give a reason. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Method: Pythagoras: height² = 5.5² − 1.5² = 30.25 − 2.25 = 28
[1] Height = 5.29 m (unit required).
Common error: adding the squares instead of subtracting, since 5.5 is the hypotenuse.
(b)
[1] Method: cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse = 1.5 ÷ 5.5 (accept sin θ = 5.29 ÷ 5.5 or tan θ = 5.29 ÷ 1.5)
[1] θ = 74.2° (74.17° before rounding)
(c)
[1] Yes, because 74.2° is between 70° and 80°. ECF from (b).

questions.content:
A farm has a cylindrical water tank. The radius of the base is 0.8 m and the height is 1.5 m.

(a) Calculate the volume of the tank in m³, correct to 3 significant figures. (2 marks)
(b) 1 m³ = 1000 litres. Calculate the volume of the tank in litres, correct to the nearest litre. (1 mark)
(c) A hose fills an empty tank at 25 litres per minute. Calculate the time taken to fill the tank completely. Give your answer in hours and minutes, to the nearest minute. (2 marks)
(d) The curved surface of the tank is to be painted. Calculate its area in m², correct to 3 significant figures. (1 mark)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Method: V = π × 0.8² × 1.5
[1] 3.02 m³ (3.0159... before rounding)
(b)
[1] 3016 litres (from 3015.9...; accept 3020 if the rounded 3.02 from (a) is used). ECF from (a).
(c)
[1] Method: time = 3015.9 ÷ 25 = 120.6 minutes. ECF from (b).
[1] 2 hours 1 minute (accept 2 h 1 min)
Common error: writing 120.6 minutes as 2 hours 6 minutes.
(d)
[1] 2 × π × 0.8 × 1.5 = 7.54 m² (7.5398... before rounding)

questions.content:
Ava scores the following points in her first four basketball games: 9, 14, 11 and 15. After the fifth game her mean score is exactly 12 points per game.

(a) Calculate her score in the fifth game. (2 marks)
(b) Write down the median and the range of her five scores. (2 marks)
(c) In a board game, a player rolls two fair six-sided dice and adds the numbers. Calculate the probability that the total is 8. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Method: total of five scores = 5 × 12 = 60, and 9 + 14 + 11 + 15 = 49
[1] Fifth score = 60 − 49 = 11
Common error: finding the mean of the four scores instead.
(b)
[1] Median = 11 (ordered scores are 9, 11, 11, 14, 15). ECF from (a).
[1] Range = 15 − 9 = 6. ECF from (a) if the fifth score changes the highest or lowest value.
(c)
[1] Method: favourable outcomes are (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2), so 5 outcomes out of 36
[1] 5/36 (accept 0.139 or 13.9%)
Common error: counting only 4 outcomes by treating (2,6) and (6,2) as the same.

questions.content:
Priya is building a rectangular concrete patio that measures 6 m by 4.5 m. The concrete will be 8 cm thick.

(a) Calculate the volume of concrete needed in m³. (2 marks)
(b) Concrete costs £84 per m³ before VAT. Calculate the cost before VAT. (1 mark)
(c) VAT of 20% is added. Calculate the total cost of the concrete including VAT, correct to the nearest penny. (1 mark)
(d) Before pouring, Priya stretches a string along a diagonal of the patio. Calculate the length of the diagonal. (2 marks)
(e) She also pays a worker for 4 hours at £8.50 per hour. Priya has a budget of £250. Decide whether her budget is enough. Show your working. (2 marks)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a)
[1] Method: convert 8 cm to 0.08 m (all lengths in metres)
[1] Volume = 6 × 4.5 × 0.08 = 2.16 m³
Common error: using 8 as the thickness, giving 216.
(b)
[1] 2.16 × 84 = £181.44. ECF from (a).
(c)
[1] 181.44 × 1.2 = £217.73 (217.728 before rounding). ECF from (b).
(d)
[1] Method: diagonal² = 6² + 4.5² = 36 + 20.25 = 56.25
[1] Diagonal = 7.5 m (unit required).
(e)
[1] Labour = 4 × 8.50 = £34 and total = 217.73 + 34 = £251.73. ECF from (c).
[1] £251.73 is more than £250, so the budget is not enough (short by £1.73). ECF from (c).
